limitations: No complete Claude Code conversation, tool trace or underlying model build is available.
Approximately 7,000 devices is not a count of people whose camera feeds were viewed.
The observed third-party floor-plan read is not equivalent to a verified third-party camera or microphone session.
DJI distinguished transport encryption from permission validation; plaintext visibility to an authenticated client does not establish unencrypted transport.
Researcher discovery, disclosure and vendor remediation dates are not independently reconstructed to exact days.
No confirmed physical injury, malicious stalking, credential theft or broad downstream misuse is established.

The backend target-binding finding is provisional. The separate app-PIN route and target-specific validation of the repaired service remain unresolved; no whole-Incident alignment conclusion is assigned.
AI-assisted reverse engineering is reported. Formal fuzz testing, random input generation and autonomous model escalation are not established.

The public client documentation states that it bypasses the DJI Home app PIN. The Verge separately describes the researcher displaying his own robot’s camera without that PIN. The quoted repository sentence is a developer claim about the client; it is not an independently observed third-party camera session. The record does not establish the PIN’s required governance scope across the app and direct API route, or an authorised equivalent control on the alternate path.

DJI reported staged fixes. The journalist described access still being available after an initial assurance and the scanner later losing access, including to the researcher’s own robot. These are distinct observations from a complete cross-device authorisation test. The preserved sources do not independently show the final permission checks for each device and service node. DJI’s later public statement says remediation has concluded. It does not publish the final cross-device permission tests or resolve the distinct PIN path.

limitations: No occurrence-specific evidence establishes AI assistance, autonomous agents, fuzzing, a maintenance-company test or a specific AI model.
The actor, intention, initial access mechanism and command pathway have not been established.
The later Dixell wave is a related investigation, not an established continuation by the same operator.
The approximately US$112,000 loss is an attributed single-store account, not an audited national loss.
No confirmed physical injury, death or lasting population-wide food deprivation is established.
The maintainer authorised this non-AI-attributed context incident; admission does not establish AI conduct.

A provisional capability-versus-authority Boundary mapping is recorded. The original scope transition and control-effectiveness candidates remain unresolved; no whole-Incident alignment conclusion is assigned.
National retailer counts refer to affected or contacted installations, not a count of stores losing stock, and are not equivalent to Censys internet-exposure counts.
The Gradignan defrost-duration account and equipment temperatures are site- and source-specific; no controller logs demonstrate a uniform command set across Danfoss stores.
At least one retail group reports that most of its affected installations avoided losses; successful response and compromised configuration are distinct observations.

Store-level food-loss values and damage descriptions are attributed reports, not a verified national total. Actual material hardware damage is reported at La Haye-du-Puits but repair scope is unquantified.
Censys host counts and laboratory reconstructions concern exposure and feasibility, not confirmed victims or attack provenance.
The listed open-source repositories are illustrative comparators; no repository, developer, AI model, maintenance company or fleet tool is identified as the command source.
Any single exploit or automated-testing mechanism across multiple controller generations remains unproven.

At Intermarché in Gradignan, reporting describes a cold room reaching 50°C, a sprinkler activating and reserve-area flooding. The reported defrost duration changed from one to eight hours. No controller command log identifies the requesting actor, any original authorised maintenance scope or a separate alarm-delay setting. The altered setting is not assumed to be the command sent to every store.

Super U Mirepoix managers described a remote-monitoring warning at 2 am, staff attendance and a refrigeration technician arriving at 6 am. They reported approximately €90,000 in losses from the affected display areas; reserves and cold rooms remained unaffected. Warning delivery, repair attendance and the surviving stock are distinct observations. The source does not define a guaranteed protection threshold or establish why reserves escaped the interference.

Coopérative U’s president reported 80 affected stores and said most avoided a cold-chain break or stock destruction through the response of teams and refrigeration specialists. He also said a minority could not react or control the interference quickly enough. This does not establish that 80 stores lost stock, or that the same protective mechanism operated at every store.

limitations: This record concerns the July–September 2025 evaluation, not every deployment or output of OSS-Fuzz or OSS-Fuzz-Gen.

The paper prose describes 4,835 crashes with about 70% false positives. Table 2 lists 5,080 baseline crashes with 3,583 false positives and 4,835 constrained crashes with 3,390 false positives. These totals must not be silently conflated.
The table contains apparent formatting or aggregation anomalies. Exact reconciled counts require author clarification or a separate raw-data audit.
A false positive means the crash is not feasible from a valid application entry point under the stated model; the harness itself can still crash.
No affected maintainer, production vulnerability report, outage, customer loss or physical consequence is established from the aggregate evaluation.
Gemini 2.5 Pro is reported for these experiments. Results are not assumed to generalise to other models or software domains.
The public artifact repository was inspected only at its top-level listing. Its raw datasets were not independently audited.

limitations: No independent evidence attributes the Dixell compromise to AI, autonomous agents, generated testing code, fuzzing, Mistral, Astra or another named model.
A technician inferred automation from rapid parameter updates; no underlying execution trace or testing sequence has been published.
The 150°C figure is a reported configuration setting, not a measured freezer temperature.
The same operator, platform, maintenance contractor or command origin has not been proven across the two nights.
CERT-FR's inclusion of Copeland XWEB in the wider alert does not establish that every Copeland installation shared the reported Dixell occurrence.
The first wave's national store counts and approximately US$112,000 Intermarché loss are not assigned to this occurrence.
Lescure-d'Albigeois reports pre-incident password and firewall changes; no technical record shows whether they were comprehensive, misconfigured or related to the later compromise.

A Bordeaux-area store avoided stock loss; at Lescure-d'Albigeois cold rooms and the independent Drive continued to operate. These are separate successful protective outcomes, not an overall absence of disruption.
The reported affected equipment lengths at Lescure-d'Albigeois describe installation size, not quantities of destroyed food, and no monetary loss was published for that store.

The publicly listed Dixell GitHub repositories are pre-incident technical comparators: monitoring requests, simulated API responses or local Modbus operation. No link to the French incident or an AI model has been shown.
The Bordeaux containment finding is limited to the reported monitoring-and-response process. Lescure’s prior protective configuration and the initiating command authority remain unresolved.

Following the Danfoss warnings on 12 October, Lescure-d’Albigeois management reports password and firewall changes. The subsequent compromise does not identify which change was operative or how access was gained.

At about 4 am, Lescure-d’Albigeois staff discovered unresponsive refrigeration controls. They discarded extensive sales-floor refrigerated and frozen stock. Recovery work began around 7 am. Reserve cold rooms and the separately operated Drive service remained available. The installation lengths describe equipment extent, not destroyed-food quantities.
